hints: Classify a quantity by deciding whether a direction is needed as well as its magnitude.
Energy, power and time need no direction; momentum and weight each have a direction.
walkthrough: A scalar is fully specified by magnitude alone, whereas a vector also needs a direction.
Energy, power and time are scalars because no direction is part of their specification.
Momentum and weight are vectors: momentum has the direction of motion, and weight acts toward the centre of the Earth.

ai_rubric.observable: Classifies energy, power and time as scalars.
Classifies momentum and weight as vectors.

hints: Treat the 120 m north and 80 m east journeys as two head-to-tail displacement vectors.
Draw the 120 m arrow north, start the 80 m east arrow at its head, then draw R from the starting point to the final point.
walkthrough: Draw a displacement arrow due north to represent the first 120 m run.
From the head of that arrow, draw the second displacement arrow due east, making a right angle between the two path vectors.
Join the initial point directly to the final point with an arrow in that direction and label this resultant displacement R.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the north and east path vectors head-to-tail at right angles, with correctly directed arrows, then draws and labels R from the start to the finish.

hints: Use the complete 27 s for both averages, but distinguish total distance travelled from displacement.
The total distance is 120 + 80 m; the resultant displacement is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with 120 m and 80 m sides.
Divide each quantity by 27 s, then use tan⁻¹(80 / 120) to give the angle measured east of the initial northward path.
walkthrough: The total time is 15 + 12 = 27 s and the total distance travelled is 120 + 80 = 200 m.
Average speed = total distance / total time = 200 / 27 = 7.41 m s⁻¹, so the average speed is 7.4 m s⁻¹.
For average velocity, use the displacement rather than the 200 m path length. The northward and eastward displacements are perpendicular.
Magnitude of average velocity = 144 / 27 = 5.33 m s⁻¹, so it is 5.3 m s⁻¹.
Measured from the initial northward direction, tan θ = 80 / 120, so θ = 33.7° ≈ 34° east of north.

ai_rubric.observable: Determines average speed as total distance 200 m divided by the total time 27 s, giving 7.4 m s⁻¹.
Combines the perpendicular 120 m and 80 m displacements to obtain a resultant of 144 m.
Divides the 144 m displacement by 27 s to obtain an average-velocity magnitude of about 5.3 m s⁻¹.
Uses the perpendicular displacement components to obtain an angle of about 34° east of the initial northward path.
